title: Arithmetic landscapes: manuscripts, Lean development and verification apparatus
notes: Licences differ by directory. Code (lean/ and the Python scripts): Apache-2.0, chosen to match Mathlib so that any lemma of general interest can go upstream without a licence change. Manuscripts (paper/): CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE.
description:
A research repository in number theory, deposited whole rather than as separate manuscripts, because the apparatus is the point.

What the mathematics says. Three manuscripts study the subset-sum landscape of a finite set A of odd integers. The ratio of strict local minima to ground states converges to a rational invariant Γ(A) read off the set by counting, and that invariant turns out to be the annealed (independence) prediction itself — so the main theorem says that the annealed count of metastable states is asymptotically exact for this model, with an explicit condition that delimits it and an explicit family that breaks it. A lower bound that would normally cost a quantitative equidistribution estimate is obtained instead from the Kubert distribution relation as an exact equality. Part II proves asymptotic flatness for the odd primes unconditionally. Part III deforms the measure, treats random sequences, and decomposes the coset energy into Dirichlet L-values.

What is in the deposit. The three manuscripts (26, 35 and 54 pp.) and a standalone note (11 pp.); a Lean 4 development of the settled results, replayed through the kernel by an independent checker that must first reject three deliberately corrupted modules; the committed scripts and logs behind every number quoted in the text; a suite of mechanical checks that runs before each commit; and a complete record of the mistakes this process has made.

What this is not. None of it is peer-reviewed, and no claim is made for it here beyond what each statement claims for itself. Every theorem, proposition and lemma declares its status — proved, derived, measured, or conjectured — at the place where it is stated. As of v1.1.0 the three headline results of Part III are unconditional; the surviving assumptions are named where they are used, and the independent reading behind the lift is described in the appendix precisely enough to say what it does not amount to.

What is new in v1.2.0, and what it corrects. This version adds a fourth manuscript: a standalone note, Two speeds at the boundary: zeros of sums of conjugate sections of power series (11 pp.), which states one question from Part III in the standard language of power series with no prerequisites from this repository and no citations to the other manuscripts at all. It also corrects four statements that were public in v1.1.1, each at its own statement and none deleted: a seven-value table wrong from the fourth significant digit; a displayed profile missing a forced clamp, which as printed did not generate the constant printed beside it; a conjectured dividing line given as summability where the mechanism itself uses only the last weight, refuted by the harmonic profile; and a refutation of our own that is withdrawn, because the band we read as evidence against a candidate is exactly what that candidate predicts at the sizes we could compute. Three of the four were found by building something new and noticing it contradicted a sentence written elsewhere, not by any mechanical check. A DOI makes a version permanent; it does not make it true.

Tool and computational resource disclosure. This work was carried out with AI language models (Anthropic's Claude) as tools, under the author's direction, following recommendation 01 for individual mathematicians of the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics (June 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.20302944), which the author has signed. Each manuscript carries a disclosure section naming the tools, the versions, and the computational resources — one personal computer, no cluster and no accelerator — and naming the provision of the Declaration that this work does not meet. Responsibility for every claim and every citation is the author's alone.
